title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: BUNNY'S CHILI
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Bunny Tate, a retired bus dispatcher from Pueblo, Colorado.
For nine years, her husband Walt won the town chili cook-off. For nine years, Bunny chopped his onions.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE SIGN-UP SHEET
segments.quote: Do one thing every day that scares you.
segments.author: Mary Schmich
lines: At sixty-four, Bunny had never cooked for a crowd.
At the hardware store, she saw the cook-off sign-up sheet, and remembered a clipping on her fridge, from the columnist Mary Schmich:
Do one thing every day that scares you.
She signed right under Walt's name. Then she sat down in the paint aisle.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE FLOPS
segments.quote: Results! Why, man, I have gotten a lot of results! I know several thousand things that won't work.
segments.author: Thomas Edison
lines: Her first pot tasted like a campfire. Her second, like a wet sock.
Walt grinned. Ready to quit, honey?
Bunny thought of Thomas Edison and his battery:
Results! Why, man, I have gotten a lot of results! I know several thousand things that won't work.
She taped a list to the cupboard. Things that won't work. She kept cooking.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: HER OWN POT
segments.quote: In order to be irreplaceable one must always be different.
segments.author: Coco Chanel
lines: By August, her chili tasted exactly like Walt's.
Her friend Rosa, who runs a taco truck by the steel mill, shrugged and quoted the designer Coco Chanel:
In order to be irreplaceable one must always be different.
So Bunny dug out Grandma's recipe card. Green chiles, cinnamon, a square of dark chocolate. It tasted like her.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE FEUD
segments.quote: I have decided to stick with love. Hate is too great a burden to bear.
segments.author: Martin Luther King Jr.
lines: Walt's bowling buddies started calling her the Competition, and stuck a Go Walt sign in her yard.
Bunny was steaming. Then she remembered a line from Martin Luther King Junior:
I have decided to stick with love. Hate is too great a burden to bear.
So she baked the bowling team cornbread. Two of them switched sides.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE WIND
segments.quote: Tough times never last, but tough people do.
segments.author: Robert H. Schuller
lines: Cook-off day, a Colorado wind blew her tent into the parking lot and dust into her pot.
She wanted to go home. Walt walked over and quoted the author Robert Schuller:
Tough times never last, but tough people do.
Then he lent her his spare pot. She started over, with a brick on the lid.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE TROPHY
segments.quote: Chains do not hold a marriage together. It is thread, hundreds of tiny threads which sew people together through the years.
segments.author: Simone Signoret
lines: Bunny won by one point. Walt cheered louder than anybody and ate three bowls.
That night, she thought of the French actress Simone Signoret:
Chains do not hold a marriage together. It is thread, hundreds of tiny threads which sew people together through the years.
Next year, they're entering as a team. Walt is chopping the onions.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Do the scary thing. Learn from flops. Be you. Choose love. Stay tough. Keep sewing.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Do the scary thing. Learn from flops. Be yourself. Choose love. Stay tough. Keep sewing.
I entered a chili contest once. The judges kept my recipe, so nobody could ever cook it again.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
